Good news — Russian citizens are visa-free for Vietnam.

- **Primary pathway:** Visa-free entry (unilateral exemption), no visa needed for short stays.
- **Key details:** Up to 45 days per visit. This exemption is currently extended through 2028-03-05 (per a March 2025 announcement). Passport must be valid for at least 180 days from the date of entry.
- **Need longer or more flexibility?** An e-Visa is also available (as it is to all nationalities) for up to 90 days, valid for air/land/sea entry across 83 approved ports, costing USD 25 (single-entry) or USD 50 (multiple-entry), with 2-3 business day processing — apply at evisa.gov.vn.
- **Data caveat:** This data is current as of 2026-08-17. Since the visa-free exemption has an expiry date, I'd recommend double-checking at evisa.gov.vn before booking travel, especially if your trip is close to or after March 2028.

Key details:

Belarusians do get visa-free entry to Vietnam under a bilateral exemption (effective Jan 30, 2025) — but it comes with a calendar-year cap, and that's the problem here.

The terms are: max 30 days per entry, and total stay not to exceed 90 days within the calendar year. You've already used 70 of those 90 days in 2026, so under the visa-free exemption you only have 20 days left this year — not the 30 you're asking for. Trying to stay 30 more would put you at 100 days for the year, 10 days over the limit.

To cover the full 30 extra days, visa-free entry won't get you there — you'd need to fall back on Vietnam's e-Visa, which is open to all nationalities regardless of the bilateral exemption's annual cap: up to 90 days per entry, costing USD 25 (single-entry) or USD 50 (multiple-entry), applied for at evisa.gov.vn (2-3 business days processing). Since you're presumably already in Vietnam on the visa-free entry, you'd typically need to exit and re-enter on the e-Visa (or check with local immigration about converting/extending your current stay) rather than just switching status in place.

One more thing worth checking directly with Vietnamese immigration: whether that 90-day figure counts stays across all entry types combined, or just visa-free entries — the dataset here only documents the visa-exemption terms, not how it interacts with a subsequent e-Visa stay in the same year.

Also note: passport must be valid at least 180 days from your entry date. Data as of 2026-08-17 — please verify current policy at evisa.gov.vn before making plans, since day-count caps like this are exactly the kind of detail that can change.

As an Indian national, you don't have visa-free access to Vietnam, and a 4-month (120-day) stay is actually too long for the standard e-Visa, which only covers up to 90 days. So for this trip you'll need an embassy/consulate visa rather than the e-Visa.

- **Pathway needed:** Embassy/consulate visa (apply through a Vietnamese embassy or consulate before you travel), in whatever category fits your purpose of visit (e.g. LV for work, DT for investment, GD for study/education-related stays, etc.). The standard tourist e-Visa tops out at 90 days, so it can't cover a 120-day stay.
- **If you can shorten the trip to 90 days or less:** you'd qualify for the e-Visa instead — apply at evisa.gov.vn, valid for stays up to 90 days, costs USD 25 (single entry) or USD 50 (multiple entry), processing takes about 2-3 business days (faster options available for a fee), and it's usable at any of Vietnam's ~83 approved entry ports (air, land, or sea) — it doesn't lock you to one specific port.
- **Passport validity:** must be valid for at least 180 days from your entry date, regardless of which route you take.
- **Data caveat:** this is based on policy data as of 2026-08-17. Visa rules can change, so please verify current requirements at https://evisa.gov.vn/ or with a Vietnamese embassy/consulate before booking your trip.
